target_customer: US and allied defense customers (Department of War, missile defense programs) buying air and missile interceptors
problem: Exquisite interceptors cost far more than the threats they defeat and magazines are shallow. Wardstone builds a low cost modular interceptor platform; its launch post describes space based kinetic interceptors, starting with a product called Hailstorm.
business_model: defense hardware contracts and development awards
product_category: missile defense interceptors and space based interceptors

founders.name: Sebastian Fischer
founders.background_notes: Per YC company page; brother of the CTO.

founders.name: Tobias Fischer
founders.background_notes: Per YC company page; was chief spacecraft engineer for a lunar CubeSat mission at Cornell.

competitors.name: Anduril and Zone 5 Technologies
competitors.what: Drone interceptor prototypes under the DIU Counter UAS NEXT program
competitors.traction_then: Successful prototype test flights and added DIU funding reported in September 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Hypersonic and ballistic intercept, propulsion, guidance and possibly space basing are research grade problems for an eight person team and need flight testing.

defensibility.rationale: Government relationships, clearances and flight heritage create barriers over time, but incumbents and well funded startups are racing for the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large primes and Anduril were already building low cost interceptors; later 2026 entrants such as Furientis and Singularity also raised money for the same wedge.

market_need_then: Interceptor cost exchange ratios and shortages were a prominent defense concern in 2025, with the DIU pushing cheaper counter UAS interceptors.

branding.domain_note: wardstone.us now redirects to wardstone.space; dates not found.

identity.logo: Not described by sources; LinkedIn says a new identity was introduced

brand_strength.rationale: A protective sounding compound name fits defense, but no source shows brand reach or press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: Wardstone entered YC in Fall 2025 with two brothers from Amazon Prime Air, Cruise, Lockheed and Astranis backgrounds, aiming to field cheap interceptors. Aggregators report a roughly $5M seed and a planned prototype flight in spring 2026, but the outcome of that flight and later funding are not confirmed. The record is early with no exit or failure signal.
notes: Unverified: aggregators (Seedtable, Extruct, Crunchbase style pages) report a $5M seed, dated either November 2025 or February 2026, with investors such as Pioneer Fund, Liquid 2 and Bow Capital; one aggregator shows $500K. No primary release or second outlet was opened, so no round is recorded. The company site wardstone.space could not be fetched because of a safety check rate limit. The YC description (modular interceptor platform) and launch post (space based interceptors) differ in emphasis.
